author: reek
body: The Lens query service, v1: the smallest program that carries a question from a wire to a warehouse and back through every governed layer. Each request is parsed into a LensQuery, planned by the grain-checked planner, rendered to T-SQL, executed through the lens-sql-exec seam, and answered as JSON. The whole program is target-independent by construction: on Target B the seam calls bind to HttpListener and SqlClient preambles, while on Target N today's seam stubs answer no requests and the loop shuts down after printing its banner, which makes the native compile an honest smoke of everything up to the wire.

author: reek
body: The request format is deliberately trivial for v1. The body is lines, each starting at the first column: dimensions: a,b then measures: x,y then limit: n, keys in any order, later lines winning, unknown lines ignored, and the lens name fixed to the demo model's. Spaces are stripped from the values rather than trimmed, so parsing depends on nothing but literal characters and behaves identically on both targets; carriage returns never reach this parser because the Target B binding strips them at the seam boundary, where barbarian line conventions belong. Filters stay out of the wire format until the service grows a real protocol; the planner machinery under this loop already handles them.

author: reek
body: On plan diagnostics the reply is the diagnostic list as a JSON array of strings instead of rows, so a caller always receives JSON and a refused query tells the analyst exactly what to fix.

author: reek
body: Two paths are special. GET /dashboard answers a complete HTML page instead of JSON, rendered by the LensDashboard chapter from results this service computed through the same plan-render-execute pipeline the query route uses. /explore is the interactive query builder: GET answers the empty form over the model's vocabulary, POST parses the form body through the LensForm chapter, runs the same pipeline, and answers the form again with the results underneath. Every other request keeps the v1 body protocol above, byte for byte.

author: reek
body: The star from the planner tests: orders is the fact table, users the dimension table, one declared many-to-one join. Revenue aggregates at the orders grain, total credit at the users grain, and the order count exercises the COUNT path end to end. The order-month dimension reads order-date, Unix seconds by the model chapter's convention, through the month bucket, so the dashboard's time tile groups by calendar month.

author: reek
body: Values strip spaces by literal replacement, and name lists split on commas with empties dropped, so a body sent with spaces after the colon or around the commas parses the same as a bare one.

author: reek
body: Result rows render as a JSON array of arrays of strings, every cell escaped for backslash and quote. Diagnostics render as a JSON array of strings in the same escape discipline.

author: reek
body: Three tiles over the demo model: revenue by city as bars, revenue by calendar month as bars over the bucketed dimension, and total credit beside revenue by city as a table. Each tile's query runs through the same pipeline as the query route - plan, render to T-SQL, execute through the seam - and the rows come back as lists of text, so the converter below rebuilds the QueryResult shape the dashboard renderer reads. The schema is built from the plan's own column order: dimension display columns first, in lp-display-cols order with bucketed dimensions under their column__bucket alias, then one column per measure under the measure's name, which is exactly the projection lp-assemble emits. Dimension cells stay text - a bucketed dimension's cells are integers spelled as text, but they are categories, not quantities - and measure cells parse to integers, because the bar charts scale by numeric column values. The converter does not divide an average's __sum and __cnt column pair; no demo tile names an average, and a dashboard that does must first grow the division lp-finish-avgs performs for lens-run. A failed plan becomes a qr-error result, which the renderer shows loud inside the tile instead of dropping it.

author: reek
body: GET /explore is the form with nothing selected and nothing run. POST /explore parses the urlencoded body into a LensQuery over this model with no filters, then walks the exact pipeline the dashboard tiles walk: plan, render to T-SQL, execute through the seam, rebuild the QueryResult from the returned text rows. A refused plan runs no SQL and hands the renderer its diagnostics as a query error, so naming no measures earns the planner's diagnostic 24 on the page with no special case here. A good run additionally hands the renderer the executed statement, so the analyst sees the grain-correct derived-table ladder Lens wrote. The converter shares the dashboard route's caveat on averages: the demo model names none, and a model that does must first grow the division lens-run performs. Everything a POST allocates - parsed form, plan, statement, rows, page - dies with the request's reply.

author: reek
body: One request at a time on port 8080: next, parse, plan, render, execute, reply. An empty answer from lens-http-next means this target has no listener behind the seam, and the loop shuts down instead of spinning on a stub. Any request for /explore and GET /dashboard reply with their pages through the HTML flavor of the reply seam; every other request takes the JSON query route unchanged.
